A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StarEmbed, with matching core data, tasks, and experiments. Their readable text, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original clustering, classification, and OOD detection results in Tables 4–6, plus appendix experiments on embedding quality, fine-tuning, and period regression.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark results and reports additional model comparisons, fine-tuning experiments, attention analyses, and synthetic forecasting experiments.

M1.justification: V4 introduces an actual architectural adaptation in a separate study: Moirai's RoPE uses observation timestamps instead of sequential indices, alongside an alternative adding time gaps as covariates (Section 5.7, Appendix A.5). V2 discusses architectural handling of irregular sampling only as future work.

E1.justification: V4 adds a bounded synthetic-data forecasting scenario using irregularly sampled sinusoids (Appendix A.5). The ZTF classes and existing MACHO diagnostic coverage remain. Period prediction is still represented by a Chronos probe in Figure 8, although v2's broader regression comparison is omitted.

E2.justification: V4 adds Moirai-2 and Time-MoE to the principal comparisons and Mantis+ and MantisV2 to clustering and classification comparisons (Tables 2–4, 8–10). Random embeddings disappear from the reported clustering tables but remain in classification and OOD comparisons. Shortened Moirai and Chronos names match the earlier small/tiny models.

E3.justification: V4 adds forecasting-versus-classification fine-tuning protocols, full/LoRA/LayerNorm adaptation settings, model-size sweeps, and LOF-based OOD evaluation. Its synthetic forecasting experiment specifies 1,000/200/200 train/validation/test samples and separate context and prediction windows. The original ZTF class counts and splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds attention-rollout case studies, adaptation-objective and parameter-efficiency comparisons, scaling analyses, an alternative OOD detector, and positional-encoding controls. Existing embedding-collapse and feature-importance analyses are retained. V2's preliminary Moirai training-loss study and full period-regression analysis are not retained.

E5.justification: V2 Table 6 reports three named seeds for RF/MLP; v4 Table 3 reports ten seeds without listing them. Both versions already describe ten-run appendix confusion matrices, so this establishes revised reporting rather than verified additional runs. V4 also adds 50% and 90% prediction intervals in forecasting plots.

E6.justification: Shared core benchmark entries remain numerically unchanged, but v4 adds substantial results for new models and analyses. For example, its new synthetic experiment reports R2 of 0.188 for timestamp-aware RoPE versus 0.016 for vanilla Moirai (Table 16). These are new experimental results, not improvements over a corresponding v2 score. V2's period-regression table and Moirai loss curve are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix B.6 and Table 20 add explicit computational-cost expressions for attention, cross-attention, feed-forward layers, and active experts, including sequence-length scaling relationships. This is a limited addition of formal complexity accounting; no theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: V2 principally presents a zero-shot benchmark and its implications for generalization. V4 expands its central contributions to adaptation objectives, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, model scaling, and timestamp-aware pre-training (Introduction and Section 6). The principal conclusions about the retained benchmark rankings remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive interpretations connecting tokenization to attention patterns, fine-tuning effectiveness to objectives and classifier expressiveness, and forecasting performance to timestamp encoding. It also introduces scaling interpretations. V2's explicit qualification that roughly 50% OOD purity still requires expert vetting is removed.

D1.justification: V4 supplies detailed adaptation recipes, synthetic-data generation settings, model specifications, trainable-parameter counts, and FLOP accounting (Appendices A and B.6). It also supplies updated dataset access information and leaderboard/Explorer links. Earlier classifier hyperparameters are largely relocated unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds discussion and citations for Moirai-2, Time-MoE, Mantis, LEAVES, attention rollout, and adaptation methods. It explicitly relates its timestamp modification to continuous-time RoPE work by Zivanovic et al. The established astronomy-baseline positioning remains; publication updates to retained references are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, model descriptions, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The contribution bullets disappear, the conclusion gains three thematic groups, and UMAP discussion and classifier settings move into reorganized appendices with a contents page. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: V4 adopts an ICML layout, merges v2 Figures 1–2, replaces the rotated classification table with an upright display, and reorganizes UMAP and timestamp illustrations. It adds attention, forecasting, scaling, and confusion-matrix displays. Some new matrix labels appear inconsistent with aggregate classification scores, notably Figure 17 versus Table 3.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens the evidence behind v2's weakly tested adaptation and irregular-sampling interpretations through controlled experiments, classification-oriented baselines, and fuller technical documentation. These benefits are tempered by removal of the full period-regression evidence and new reporting inconsistencies: Figure 17's Time-MoE/MLP matrix implies approximately 0.881 accuracy using its printed class labels and Table 1 counts, whereas Table 3 reports 0.758. The revision therefore provides a qualified, limited net improvement despite its substantial expansion.
